newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rules out changes in BP contract.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rules out changes in BP contract.

text.p: Colombia has ruled out making any changes in the terms of an association contract under which British Petroleum Co Plc was granted the right to develop the Piedemonte block in its eastern plains, a top government official said.

Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar said President Ernesto Samper had decided against revising the "sliding scale" contract, which BP's local subsidiary, BP Exploration Company (Colombia) Ltd, has described as economically unworkable.
"A signed contract is a contract that sticks," Villamizar told reporters of Samper's decision.
"The Piedemonte contract will not be modified," he said.
He stressed, however, that the decision did not rule out possible "additional and parallel agreements" aimed at making development of the Piedemonte fields more attractive for BP in the future.
Villamizar did not elaborate, but said such add-on agreements could include "economic incentives" that were not included in the original contract.

Under the existing contract, profits from the field are divided equally between BP and the state oil company Ecopetrol when total production is less than 60 million barrels. But Ecopetrol's share rises gradually as production increases, topping out at 76 percent when it reaches 150 million barrels.

BP spokesmen are reluctant to explain why they signed the contract in the first place, since they say it cuts their profit margin to no more than about eight to 12 percent over the life of the contract, well below the internationally accepted benchmark of 15 to 20 percent.

Piedemonte is estimated to contain between 600 million to one billion barrels of crude oil and condensates. But the very deep reservoir depth, averaging between between 15,000 and 18,000 feet, is expected to make drilling costs high. -- Javier Mozzo, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944
